provenance.l: JAXA — H3/MMX launch plan, Aug 2026 (H3-24L: first stage 240 t / 224.5 t propellant (maximum) / 2,942 kN, second stage 28 t / 24.6 t, SRB-3 76.2 t each, L fairing 16.4 m 2.7 t; event table with altitude and inertial speed: SRB-3 sep 116/118 s, fairing 197 s at 131 km, MECO 292 s at 208 km / 6.2 km/s, SECO1 640 s at 329 km / 7.7 km/s; MMX 4,480 kg)
JAXA — H3 F9 press kit (LE-9 1,471 kN vacuum, 422 s; LE-5B-3 137 kN, 448 s; SRB-3 2,300 kN max, 283.6 s)
ESA — MMX lifts off to Mars's moon Phobos (H3 F10, 20 Oct 2026 JST; the second stage made the Mars-transfer burn)

Stage 1 flies the plan's 2,942 kN vacuum (Table 3). The 224.5 t is the maximum load: 711 kg/s burns 207.6 t by MECO at 292 s, the rest rides in dryKg (15.5 t structure + 16.9 t unburned). The pitch table is fitted to Table 2's altitude and inertial speed (MECO 208 km / 6.2 km/s, SECO1 640 s at 329 km / 7.7 km/s), the parking orbit is SECO1's 329 km. SRB-3 thrust is the burn average over the ~110 s burn; LE-9 sea-level thrust and Isp are estimated from the vacuum figures (not published)
